biphase_mark_code_waveform.summary: Bi-phase Mark Code is a Manchester variant with TWO cells per data bit. Cell 1 of every data bit toggles relative to the previous cell (= transition at every bit boundary). For a '1', cell 2 also toggles (= mid-bit transition). For a '0', cell 2 does not toggle (= no mid-bit transition).
biphase_mark_code_waveform.dc_balance: DC-balanced over time because every bit boundary has a transition.
biphase_mark_code_waveform.polarity_independence: Inverting the BMC stream yields the same decoded data — the receiver can lock without knowing absolute polarity.
biphase_mark_code_waveform.clock_recovery: The bit clock can be recovered from the BMC transitions themselves; no separate clock line is required.

Z.purpose: Channel-A subframe start of frame 1 of a block — block boundary.

X.purpose: Channel-A subframe start — frames 2-192 within a block.

preamble_waveforms_bmc_cells.rule: Each preamble is 8 BMC cells = 4 data-bit times wide. The three patterns each contain a three-cell-long pulse, deliberately violating BMC's 'transition every bit boundary' rule; this guarantees they cannot collide with valid BMC data and serve as unambiguous frame markers.

field_bit_offsets.purpose: X / Y / Z BMC-violating long pulses for subframe alignment
Optional 4 LSBs of 24-bit audio sample, or ancillary data
20-bit audio (LSB at bit 8, MSB at bit 27)
Even parity over bits 4-30 of the same subframe

block_timing.block_boundary_marker: Preamble Z appears on the channel-A subframe of frame 1 of every block; X appears on the channel-A subframe of frames 2-192.
block_timing.channel_status_word_complete: After 192 successive C-bits per channel, the 192-bit channel-status word for that channel is reassembled.
block_timing.user_data_word_complete: After 192 successive U-bits per channel, the 192-bit user-data word for that channel is reassembled.

general_timing_rule: All timing is scaled to the sample rate. The frame rate equals the sample rate (one frame per sample). The data bit rate equals 64 × sample rate (64 data bits per frame: 2 subframes × 32 bits). The BMC cell rate equals 128 × sample rate (2 BMC cells per data bit). The receiver recovers clock from the BMC transitions and uses the X / Y / Z preambles to align subframe / frame / block boundaries.
